title: infrastructure-weekly-update-2026-09-28
content:
Summary:
This week focused on fleet health following last week's driver rollout, regional capacity forecasting for the next quarter, and finalizing the procurement plan for NPU/GPU refresh. Key items: node replacement progress, spot vs. reserved mix adjustments, and failed-job analysis for long-tail latencies.

Fleet health and incidents:
- Driver/ CUDA patch rollout: Completed staged rollouts in us-west1 and eu-west1 on 2026-09-26. No major regressions; saw a 0.8% increase in preemptible eviction handling after kernel update (expected).
- Ongoing incident: intermittent OOMs on 80GB instances when serving long-context LLMs (> 32k). Root cause narrowed to a kernel memory accounting bug under our custom kernel-build (JIRA-INFRA-1123). Temporary mitigation: enforce per-container RLIMIT_AS and reduce max_concurrent_sessions on affected pools.
- Node replacements: RMA and replacement of 12 faulty A100 nodes in us-east1 completed. 4 replacement nodes still pending (backorder ETA 2026-10-05).

Capacity & regional planning:
- Current fleet (global): 1,560 total GPUs (mix: A100-80GB: 520, A100-40GB: 420, H100: 300, T4/V100: 320).
- Usages this week: avg utilization 62% global; p95 latency capacity pressure observed in eu-west1 during APAC morning window (5:00-7:00 UTC).
- Forecast for Q4 (conservative): expected demand ramp of +28% token throughput driven by new customer onboarding (predictable from trial-to-paid conversion trends). We need an additional ~360 effective 40GB-equivalent GPUs to keep the cushion at 20% if current batching/caching remains unchanged.
- Action: short-term plan to shift 40 additional A100-40GB equivalents from reserved to burstable dedicated pools and increase prefix cache retention for high-traffic customers (expected to reduce demand by ~8%).

Autoscaling and cost controls:
- Autoscaling tuning: reduced scale-down cooldown from 10m to 5m for dedicated pools experiencing oscillation. This reduced thrash but increases transient cost by ~1.2%. Monitoring for 2 weeks before finalizing.
- Spot/preemptible strategy: increasing spot usage in non-SLA workloads to 65% (from 55%) to offset backlog for Dedicated customers. Implemented smarter fallback routing to prevent increased tail latency for high-priority routes (JIRA-INFRA-1150).

Performance and reliability metrics:
- Mean time between FAILURE (MTBF) improved by ~7% month-over-month after firmware and power-cycling automation.
- Job-level tail latencies: identified a subset of inference jobs (long-context chat sessions) with token-generation stalls after 1,000 tokens - correlates with KV cache eviction patterns. Next week will run a focused A/B with extended KV cache retention for 2 high-volume customers.

Procurement and hardware roadmap:
- Procurement: final quote received for H100 refresh; negotiating price and lead-times with two vendors. Preliminary plan: stagger H100 arrival across Nov-Jan to smooth onboarding.
- Edge/Region expansion: evaluating us-central-2 (OCI region partner) for Dedicated customers in central US to reduce transit costs and improve p95 latency for Midwest customers. PoC to be scheduled in Oct.

Operational tasks & workstreams:
- Capacity planning model: deploying new demand signal inputs (billing-trial conversion, SE pipeline handoff events) into the model to reduce underprovisioning. Expected rollout 2026-10-12.
- Maintenance windows: planned firmware upgrades in eu-west1 on 2026-10-03 (4:00-6:00 UTC). Will use rolling upgrades with traffic draining; customers notified via console.
- Runbook updates: updated OOM and kernel bug mitigation steps; added automated rollback playbook for driver rollouts.

Risks & blockers:
- Replacement node backorder could push full capacity recovery into mid-October if vendors slip. Contingency: increase temporary borrowing from partner region pools.
- Kernel memory accounting bug needs a patch from kernel-build team; temporary mitigations increase operational complexity and may affect short-term availability.

Action items (owners):
- Tom Chen: coordinate vendor timelines and finalize staggered H100 procurement schedule (due 2026-10-04).
- Aisha Patel: run A/B for extended KV cache retention for two customers and report metrics (due 2026-10-06).
- Miguel Ortiz: finalize and test autoscaler cooldown tuning in staging and promote if stable (due 2026-09-30).
- Priya Nair: complete runbook additions and publish to Confluence (due 2026-09-29).

Meeting notes (weekly sync 2026-09-28):
- Attendees: Tom, Aisha, Miguel, Priya, Elena.
- Discussion: prioritized H100 procurement cadence vs. inventory smoothing; agreed to stagger deliveries and keep flexible capacity in us-west1 as a hot spare. Decided to accelerate the KV cache A/B to inform Q4 capacity model.
- Decisions: roll back change that increased per-container memory limit for non-Dedicated pools until kernel patch lands.

Notes to self / open questions:
- Confirm whether engineering-allocations for internal load (benchmarks and CI) can be throttled to free up ~10 GPUs during peak rollout windows.
- Validate cost impact of increasing spot allocation to 65% for non-SLA workloads (finance modeling).

Attachments / links:
- Jira: JIRA-INFRA-1123 (kernel memory accounting), JIRA-INFRA-1150 (autoscaler tuning).
- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/487 (autoscaler backoff tuning).
- Confluence: infra/gpu-procurement-2026 (procurement quotes and vendor comparison).

Next update: 2026-10-05

-- End of update --
